answer: An agent market requires each identity to lock $100 of collateral for 30 days before it can bid on jobs, with one active bid allowed per deposit. Calling three agents sable, comet and willow creates no extra capacity unless each has its own locked funds. An attacker running 10,000 identities must immobilize $1 million for a month. The rule makes disposable identities costly in capital and lost interest, while keeping the cost tied to simultaneous bidding power.
